title: Delhi Man Hunts Down Scammer Using ChatGPT, Makes Him Beg For Forgiveness: 'Maa Kasam, Ab Nahi Karunga' | Viral News - News18
text: Scams are at an all-time high with the advancement in technology. Scammers are reaching out to potential victims through increasingly sophisticated methods, including spoofed phone calls and text messages, fake invoices and emails and social media. But a man recently outsmarted a scammer and made him beg for forgiveness by using ChatGPT. Wondering how? Posted under the title “Used ChatGPT to locate a scammer and made him beg me" on Reddit, the man shared how he created a fake payment link that captured the fraudster’s geolocation and a photograph of his face. What Happened? The incident began when he received a Facebook message from someone posing as his college senior, an IAS officer, offering “Army transfer/cheap goods." The scammer claimed a “CRPF officer friend" was being relocated and was selling premium appliances and furniture at heavily discounted rates. But he immediately grew suspicious because his actual senior already had his phone number. After confirming it on WhatsApp, he realised, “It was a fraud." Instead of ignoring or blocking the fake profile, he decided to play along to expose the scammer’s operation. The scammer soon contacted him via a different number, sporting a profile picture of someone in an army uniform. He sent a QR code to demand payment, urging him to send the money quickly. Instead of paying, the Delhi man used ChatGPT to build a simple but functional webpage to quickly code a geolocation/front-camera capture link. He sent the link to the scammer, telling him that uploading the QR code there would ‘expedite the payment process’ Driven by greed and urgency, the scammer clicked the link. The man instantly received the scammer’s precise GPS location, IP address, and even “a clear, front-camera snapshot of him sitting." He then sent the scammer the collected details. What followed was pure chaos. Scammer Panicked Completely in shock, the scammer began calling repeatedly from multiple numbers, pleading for mercy. He begged the man not to escalate the matter, at one point promising, “Maa kasam, ab nahi karunga ye kaam.’ ‘AI Used For The Right Reasons’ The post quickly went viral, with the internet applauding his ingenuity in using AI for scam prevention. “Mad respect. I am going to use this. In fact, make this open source. Host it somewhere so that we can do it too," wrote a Reddit user. Another commented, “AI used for the right reasons. Good work!" “Only if our cops can be this efficient. Mad respect," said a user. An individual stated, “Absolutely well done! You just nailed it. While I was reading the post, I was literally laughing a lot. We have been hearing these kinds of stories these days, and the scammers are rapidly increasing and approaching in multiple ways." “I think there is more to this than simply asking ChatGPT to write code. Maybe someone with your IT background could handle it. The creators of ChatGPT likely implemented limits on its capabilities. Without these restrictions, it would be too easy for someone to trick a non-IT person into revealing sensitive information such as geolocation or access to the front camera," read a comment. An account remarked, “Wow. This is amazing! I didn’t even know this could be done. Great job!!" Though the man admitted the scammer would return to his schemes soon, he expressed the thrill of the moment, saying, “The satisfaction of stealing from a thief is crazy."
